articles.title: Do we really need clothes delivered in under an hour? Target’s Uber Eats deal is convenience culture gone wild | Maggie Zhou
articles.summary: The time lag between ordering a meal and its packaging hitting your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief. Will items bought through this partnership be treated differently?
body: I n a move nobody outside of boardrooms asked for, Target has become the first fashion retailer in Australia to make their products available to order via the Uber Eats app as of September. This means that a “curated” selection of 25,000 of Target’s products can arrive at your door in under an hour, thanks to Uber Eats’ “on-demand” delivery.

It follows Bunnings introduction to the platform in February, with Kmart potentially following suit. Big W has also joined in on the action, with more than 35,000 Big W “essentials” (their words, not mine) now ready to be delivered to your home in 60 minutes via Doordash.

You can buy women’s heels, fashion jewellery, pyjamas and men’s suits, jocks and Christmas merch. You can buy homewares, baby goods, accessories, toys and beauty products, too. This sits side-by-side with Uber Eats’ main offerings of, well, things you can eat.

Each year, the average Australian buys 56 new clothing items and sends 23kg of textile to waste. Instead of being cherished, passed-down and respected, Clothes are increasingly seen as disposable. Garments displayed next to your weekly grocery shop or hangover order is the most explicit and unabashed pronouncement of this.
points: The time lag between ordering a meal and its packaging hitting your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief.
Will items bought through this partnership be treated differently?

articles.title: A job that changed me: On midnight shifts as a Subway ‘sandwich artist’ I served clubbers, cops and sailors
articles.summary: In Perth’s nightlife precinct in the 1990s, I made a lot of sandwiches – but the sandwiches also made me. Delivering pizzas, with all due respect, was a cruisy gig that fit in with my uni commitments.
body: The job’s biggest downside was that it didn’t pay much, especially once you factored in the costs of fuel and vehicle maintenance. So I applied for a job as a “sandwich artist” at Subway in Northbridge, Perth’s nightlife district. I figured that switching to a job where I was on my feet instead of on the road would significantly extend the life expectancy of my hand-me-down Mitsubishi Magna.

Working at Subway was more demanding than navigating apartment block intercoms and trying not to forget people’s garlic bread. Bins needed to be emptied. Bread was baked daily. Tables were continually sprayed and wiped. Salads and fillings required washing, slicing and cooking. Kind of. For one particular sandwich filling, I squeezed biblical amounts of mayo on to shredded seafood extender and massaged the lot by hand.
None of this was roquette science but that didn’t stop me from finding pride in being a tiny, hard-working cog in the restaurant machine.
I spent almost two years working from midnight till 5am every Saturday and experienced the full spectrum of late-night characters out and about in Perth.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Orlando was paralysed and almost died – then became the perfect guide dog
articles.summary: He had tetanus and I was brokenhearted when it seemed as if he wouldn’t pull through. But he worked hard, made a full recovery and helped to change someone’s life. When I first met Orlando, he was about eight weeks old.
body: Dogs aren’t vaccinated against tetanus because it is so rare, and I don’t think I realised how unwell Orlando was. For the first week it was terrifying. He became completely paralysed and I was awake every night expecting a call to say that he had died. He was too sick to carry on training as a guide dog. He had to learn how to eat, walk and do almost everything again.

When he came back to live with me, he couldn’t go up the stairs. We had to put mats on the floor, because if he slid it would hurt him, and he could manage only short walks. He was very demanding – he had a unique high-pitched bark and he’d tell you what he wanted. You could be sitting in a cafe and he’d tell you: that’s it, we’ve had enough of sitting, it’s time to go. He was also very cheeky. He’d take my daughter’s smelly socks and then give me a look as if to say, “What? I didn’t do it.”

People were always asking after him. He was very resilient and determined – you can’t get much more inspiring than Orlando. He stayed with us until he was 17 months old, and then I gave him to his trainer from Guide Dogs. I felt very emotional, but also proud. It is like your child going off to university.
points: He had tetanus and I was brokenhearted when it seemed as if he wouldn’t pull through.
But he worked hard, made a full recovery and helped to change someone’s life.

articles.title: Is it Safe to Travel to Paris Right Now Amidst the France Protests?
articles.summary: As France protests and unrest continue unfolding across the capital, we share practical advice on where to stay, what to avoid, and how to navigate the city safely.
body: If there is one thing that the French know how to do, it is fight for their rights. It’s not for the goodness of politicians' hearts that university fees in France are still $200 for a bachelor's degree but thanks to a population that refuses to back down when their rights are being threatened.

Since September, French high school students have been protesting for better conditions, especially in suburban areas often forgotten by institutions. The movement has reached almost unprecedented proportions, with other sectors joining the students, demanding better learning conditions and fighting against the cost-of-living crisis, hike in fuel prices, and erosion of social welfare.
Demonstrators gather across Paris as part of a broader protest movement over rising living costs and college tuition.

articles.title: Crispy Potato Caesar Salad
articles.summary: When I think about my dream roast potato (doesn’t everybody?), it’s shatteringly crisp on the outside, probably roasted in rendered chicken fat. It’s golden-brown all over with craggy edges to catch bits of garlic and seasonings, and yet the inside is impossibly tender and fluffy.
body: Make Caesar salad with a Greek yogurt-lightened dressing and shatteringly crisp, craggy potatoes instead of croutons.

So, instead of fresh croutons — which are still delicious — I went ahead and made my dream potatoes and used those instead for a truly transcendent Caesar salad experience. And yes, okay, sure, when it comes to effort, the perfect potatoes do come at a slightly steeper price than baked bread. You parboil them, rough up the edges a bit, and roast them for about an hour, moving them around every so often for maximum browning. The results, however, more than make up for the investment.

And to keep things fair, the dressing is relatively fuss-free, with mayo and Greek yogurt as the base (not traditional, but it lightens things up and goes great with the potatoes), and fish sauce in place of anchovies so you don’t have to crack open the tin and chop them up. It’s so savory, special, and simple that I can’t believe I didn’t try this years ago.

articles.title: Forget Lasagna: Million Dollar Spaghetti Is So Much Easier
articles.summary: I love lasagna as much as the next person, but a really good lasagna is a labor of love. So when you don’t have the time to make the layered dish, thankfully there’s million dollar spaghetti.
body: Million dollar spaghetti has got it all: saucy Bolognese, tender noodles, and tons and tons of cheese. It’s also a breeze to throw together. The sauce starts off with an onion and garlic base (no good sauce is complete without one), and the carrots and celery add a bit more bite and texture to the dish. A combination of ground meat and Italian sausage adds even more depth of flavor. ( As a vegetarian, I swapped in Beyond ground meat and Italian sausage, and it was just as delicious.) Three different types of cheese add creaminess, and fresh basil and parsley add a bright, herbaceous note.

The easiest part is, rather than fussing with lasagna sheets you just build your layers with cooked spaghetti. Simply bake until it is golden-brown and bubbly, and the cheese has fully melted. It couldn’t be easier! I always love to go for those corner pieces where the cheese and pasta form a little crust and you get even more chew. It’s a total crowd-pleaser, and makes a lot so it’s enough to feed the whole family and still have leftovers.
points: I love lasagna as much as the next person, but a really good lasagna is a labor of love.
So when you don’t have the time to make the layered dish, thankfully there’s million dollar spaghetti.

articles.title: I’ve Finally Found the Fall Shoes That Look Best With Jeans
articles.summary: Whether you’re staying comfy in your barrel jeans or shimmying into a skinny style this fall, the brown ballerina flat is your denim’s best friend.
body: No matter how many times we’ve seen bloomers in the streets, a tailored trouser envisioned by every designer across fashion weeks the world over, and celebrities trying out the skant —the truth is, jeans remain the enduring, trend-transcending icon of any closet. But this fall, we’re taking it to ground level: you might have mastered your perfect denim, but what about the shoes to go with?

Kate Middleton —Catherine, Princess of Wales—is a fan of earth-toned ballet flats, pairing them with her tailored pants for an elegant, versatile look. Katie Holmes has been spotted more than once in a textured, woven pair from the super affordable Dune, which she has styled with dark gray straight leg jeans, a cosy gray rollneck sweater, and thick black socks. Didn’t think these shoes would suit some tubing? Holmes is here to prove you wrong, with a styling tip that keeps this combo going into winter. Right now, I personally love wearing the Sport Jean (also loved by Zoë Kravitz ) from Still Here in milk white with the Le Monde Béryl Luna Slipper in a dark espresso shade for some contrast.
points: Whether you’re staying comfy in your barrel jeans or shimmying into a skinny style this fall, the brown ballerina flat is your denim’s best friend.

articles.title: New York, New York—Why We All Want To Be A Part of It
articles.summary: Who didn't want to claim the city as their won this year? Upper West Sider Gary Shteyngart rhapsodizes on why this is NYC's moment (the Knicks are just the start of it) and why it deserves a top spot on this year's Readers' Choice Awards.
body: As an almost lifelong citizen of New York City in his mid-50s, I go through the usual phases of “What have they done to my beloved city?” and “Hmm, things aren't as bad as I thought they were.” Right now I'm definitely in the second stage of my relationship with Gotham. What's changed? The answer nearly everyone gives is “da Knicks.” I'm not a huge sports fan, but when it felt like the whole city was dancing around me and Spike Lee was throwing block parties in Fort Greene, it was hard not to get caught up in the joy. And then, to up the good-vibes ante, the World Cup came our way, and Norwegian soccer fans were Viking-rowing in Times Square.

What this means to me on a day-by-day level is that, because of this economic and cultural diversity, New York is still the best walking city in America and perhaps the world. The Italians have their evening passeggiata, and Spaniards practice the splendid art of the tapear, hopping from tapas joint to tapas joint in search of satisfaction and tipsiness. I head out on great all-around-the-world culinary feasts, which can be found in nearly every corner of New York.
points: Who didn't want to claim the city as their won this year?

articles.title: “It’s A Mindset”: Rosie Huntington-Whiteley On Returning To Victoria’s Secret 16 Years Later
articles.summary: “It’s really about consistency because I’m a gym girl,” says Rosie Huntington-Whiteley of preparing for her Victoria’s Secret runway comeback 16 years after she hung up her wings.
body: Twenty years ago, a 19-year-old Devon native named Rosie Huntington-Whiteley made her Victoria’s Secret runway debut in a polka-dot bra and briefs, carrying a stuffed polka-dot dog, with a polka-dot duvet trailing behind her. This cutesy girl-next-door look helped to catapult Huntington-Whiteley from Teen Vogue favourite to Burberry face, bona fide lingerie designer, beauty entrepreneur and blockbuster movie star. Now, after hanging up her Angel wings in 2010 to focus on building her own Rose Inc empire, she’s back in the Victoria’s Secret fold.
With Izabel Goulart, Selita Ebanks and Miranda Kerr in Times Square in 2009.

articles.title: I Tried the 'Normatec Go' Compression Boots, and My Calves Have Never Felt Better
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. If you've ever been on your feet all day and your calves felt like two sandbags, you know how tough it can be to find relief. I'm a marathon runner, so I know it well. Training blocks mean high mileage, and calves take a beating on every mile.
body: This week's upgrade is the first recovery tool that seems to do all the work for me, and hey—after a long run, I'm not complaining. It's my first foray into compression boots: the Hyperice Normatec Go.

The Normatec Go is a pair of wearable compression sleeves that wrap around your calves and give you a dynamic air compression massage. Hyperice describes it as a fully portable version of its Normatec line, which pro athletes and recovery rooms have used for years.

The sleeves inflate and deflate in a pulsing pattern (as opposed to just squeezing constantly). Hyperice calls this compression "gapless": There are three overlapping zones of 360-degree compression working through the calf. In theory, the wave of pressure helps push fluid and blood through your lower legs, which is why Hyperice says the massage increases circulation and reduces tension and swelling.

Hyperice also points out that the calf is often called the body's "second heart" because it helps push blood back up from your lower legs. That matches my experience: After a long run, calves are where the heaviness and tightness show up first.
